dotyczący pasterstwa, związany z pasterstwem

examples.text: W szałasie pasterskim poczęstowano wszystkich żentycą.

glosses: leżący w gestii biskupa lub episkopatu, odnoszący się do ich posługi

examples.text: W liście pasterskim biskupi przypomnieli o roli rodziny.

glosses: Of or pertaining to shepherds or herders of other livestock.

examples.text: Like the Mesolithic age of 10,000-8000 B.C., the period 6000-4000 B.C. seems to be one of the fall of fortresses and the rise of pastoral nomadism.

glosses: Relating to rural life and scenes, in particular of poetry.

examples.text: We were living a pastoral life.
[…] these pastoral farms, / Green to the very door; and wreaths of smoke / Sent up, in silence, from among the trees!

There was a tone, too, of pastoral poetry shed over the new scenes to which they were just introduced, that had a greater effect from the contrast to those, artificial and crowded, which they had just left.
He wanders west as far as Memphis, a solitary migrant upon that flat and pastoral landscape.

glosses: Relating to the care of souls, to the pastor of a church or to any local religious leader charged with the service of individual parishioners, i.e. a priest or rabbi.

examples.text: pastoral duties
a pastoral letter

“In terms of pastoral consequences,” Cardinal Víctor Manuel Fernández, who leads the Vatican’s office on doctrine, said in a news conference Monday, “the principle of welcoming all is clear in the words of Pope Francis.”

glosses: A poem describing the life and manners of shepherds; a poem in which the speakers assume the character of shepherds; an idyll; a bucolic.

examples.text: Ethel was silent from surprise: she had prepared herself for anger—even sorrow; but ridicule left her without an answer. What could she say to a hearer, who only smiled, and to whom emotion was only a scene in a pastoral?

glosses: A cantata relating to rural life; a composition for instruments characterized by simplicity and sweetness; a lyrical composition the subject of which is taken from rural life.
A letter of a pastor to his charge; specifically, a letter addressed by a bishop to his diocese.
A letter of the House of Bishops, to be read in each parish.
